To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

operando hard X- ray spectro-imaging with a new data analysis method enables visualization of electrochemically-driven solid-state phase transformations at the nanoscales, and that mechanistic insights are obtained for a conversion cathode material, which are crucial for realizing high-capacity Li-ion batteries.

operando visualization of electrochemical phase transformations at the nanoscales can be achieved by combining hard X-ray spectro-microscopy with a new data analysis method, and that this method is particularly useful in studying conversion reactions of iron fluoride, where we observe a more complete discharge, faster and more homogeneous phase transformations in porous polycristalline samples.

operando visualization of electrochemically induced solid-state phase transformations is possible using a new method that enables visualization of weakly absorbing materials, and that this method can be used to reveal the mechanism of electrochemical reactions in conversion cathode materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods and their application to the understanding of electrochemical phase transformations in battery materials.
the visualization of solid-state phase transformations.
the development of a new data analysis method for operando hard X-rays spectro-imaging, and its application in understanding the reaction mechanism of conversion cathode materials.

operando hard X-Ray spectro-imaging can be used to study solid-state phase transformations at the nanoscales and provide mechanistic insights to the reaction dynamics of conversion-type electrode materials.

the operando visualization of the electrochemical reaction dynamics and the solid-state phase transformations at the nanoscales in the weakly absorbing iron fluoride cathode materials has been achieved by the new data analysis method.
the operando visualization of the electrochemical reaction dynamics at nanoscale is achieved by the data analysis method for weakly absorbing samples.

we have developed a novel data analysis method for operando hard X- ray spectro-imaging to visualize weakly absorbing samples, and applied it to study electrochemical reaction mechanisms of conversion cathode materials.
operando visualization of solid-state phase transformations is now possible at the nanoscales for a broad range of materials.

we have developed an in situ X-ray spectro-imager for studying electrochemical reactions in weakly absorbing samples, and used it to visualize the reaction dynamics in a conversion cathode material, iron fluoride, with unprecedented spatial resolution.

the operando visualization of solid-state phase transformations is no longer limited to samples with strong absorption.
operando visualization of electrochemically-driven phase transformations in weakly absorbing materials is possible using hard X-ray spectroscopic techniques.
